summary: Same pattern — four stationary rainbow bands undulating under a vertical travelling wave — but the port's undulation is only ~59% as deep, travels UP the grid where the original's travels DOWN, cycles ~25% faster, and the port adds a 'Columns' slider the original does not have.
observations: Rig is 2D grid 16x16 (default). Both sides compile and run clean, no runtime errors, on every window tried (6 s, 24 s, 60 s, 300 s, and a late window at t=120-132 s). Neither side decays, freezes or saturates: brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 1 (the unavoidable first frame) on both.

STRUCTURE (identical on both sides): four bright vertical bands separated by dark gaps (dominant spatial brightness harmonic k=4 across the width on both), with hue making exactly ONE full rainbow turn across the width (measured hue turns per row: orig 1.07, port 1.08 at 16x16; 1.02 vs 1.04 at 32x32). Band order left-to-right red -> yellow/green -> cyan -> blue/purple on both. Neither side scrolls horizontally: the DC term of the band offset sits at -1.45 px (orig) / -1.53 px (port) and stays there over 24 s.

MOTION AXIS (the divergence): each row's bands are displaced horizontally by an amount that varies sinusoidally with y, and that y-wave travels vertically. Tracking the wave crest's row index at 16x16, 0.25 s apart: ORIG 5.9 -> 6.6 -> 7.4 -> 8.5 -> 9.7 -> 10.8 -> 11.9 -> 12.9 -> ... -> 15, wraps to 0 and climbs again (crest moves DOWNWARD, top to bottom, ~3.5 rows/s). PORT 4.8 -> 4.2 -> 3.4 -> 2.1 -> 1.0 -> 0, wraps to 15 and keeps descending (crest moves UPWARD, bottom to top, ~3.6 rows/s). Reconfirmed independently at 32x32 (orig crest y 12 -> 20 -> 28 -> 30 over t=0..3 s; port crest y 10 -> 2 -> 30 -> 24 over the same times). The travel SPEED magnitude matches (~0.22-0.25 rig-heights/s on both); only the sign is flipped.

AMPLITUDE: the peak-to-peak horizontal displacement of the bands is much smaller on the port. At 16x16 over a 24 s / 96-frame track the median peak-to-peak swing is orig 5.19 px vs port 3.03 px. At 32x32 (t=0..3 s) orig spans -8.9..+2.0 = 10.9 px (34% of the width) vs port -6.7..-0.3 = 6.4 px (20%). Ratio orig:port = 1.70 at both sizes, i.e. the port's bands are ~41% straighter. This is plainly visible in the 32x32 contact sheets: the original draws bold S-curves, the port draws gentle wiggles.

TEMPORAL PERIOD: autocorrelation of the row-0 band displacement gives orig 6.25-6.50 s and port 5.00 s, identically at --fps 10, 20 and 40. Correspondingly the y-wavelength of the undulation is ~1.4 x grid height on the original and ~1.2 x grid height on the port (sinusoid fits: orig lambda_y median ~23 rows, port ~19 rows at 16x16).

COLOR/BRIGHTNESS: same palette family and same saturation ballpark, port marginally darker and crisper. meanBrightness 62 (orig) vs 56 (port) on every window; mean per-pixel max-channel value 114.6 vs 105.1; fraction of near-black pixels (V<16) 10.8% vs 13.9%; fraction of near-saturated pixels (V>200) 17.5% vs 14.5%; mean saturation 0.905 vs 0.925. Value histograms otherwise have the same continuous shape - no clipping or collapse on either side.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes NO controls at all (meta.json sides.orig.controls == []). The port exposes one: sliderColumns, kind 'slider', label 'Columns'. The probe rates it strongly responsive (maxDelta 66.7, maxDeltaLit 67.0).

The port's untouched default render is BYTE-IDENTICAL to sliderColumns=0.5, and that setting produces 4 bands - i.e. the invented dial's default does reproduce the original's band count, so the untouched comparison is fair.

FPS INVARIANCE: both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped. The 6.4 s (orig) / 5.0 s (port) cycle and the ~5.2 px / ~3.0 px swings are unchanged at --fps 10, 20 and 40. No frame-rate coupling bug on either side.
SEED INDEPENDENCE: t=0 frames are byte-identical across --seed 1, 7 and 1234 on BOTH sides. The pattern is fully deterministic; no stochastic element to judge.

RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE: both sides behave the same way under rig overrides - hue still makes 1 turn per row and the band count stays 4 at 8x8, 16x16, 32x8 and 32x32, and the wave swing stays a fixed FRACTION of the width on each side (orig 27.6/28.8/28.4%, port 19.9/19.7/19.1% at 8x8 / 32x32 / 32x8). So the amplitude gap is a property of the port, not of the lens.

NO REGIME STRUCTURE: a 300 s / 4 fps survey shows a homogeneous rhythm image on both sides - no mode rotation, no palette walk, no long super-cycle. The 60 s survey and the t=120-132 s late window show the same amplitudes and the same travel directions as t=0, so the steady state matches the opening seconds on both sides.

dials.name: sliderColumns
dials.origEffect: control does not exist on the original (original exposes zero controls)
dials.portEffect: live and strongly value-dependent: sets the number of bright bands across the width in unit steps. Frame-hash clustering over 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625, 0.75, 0.875, 1 gives 7 distinct looks with dominant spatial harmonic k = 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7 (0 and 0.125 byte-identical; 0.875 and 1 byte-identical). Hue still makes exactly one rainbow turn across the width at every setting, and the wave amplitude is unaffected (swing 2.95-3.17 px across the whole sweep). Default = 0.5 = 4 bands = the original's geometry.

feedback: Reverse the vertical travel direction of the undulation. The original's wave crest migrates from the top of the grid toward the bottom (crest row 5.9 -> 15 over ~3.5 s at 16x16, then wraps); the port's migrates bottom-to-top (crest row 4.8 -> 0 over ~1.25 s, then wraps to 15). Flipping the sign of the time term (or of the y term) inside the wave argument is the whole fix - the travel SPEED is already right (~0.22-0.25 rig-heights per second on both sides).

Increase the undulation amplitude by ~1.7x. The horizontal displacement of the bands should span ~34% of the rig width peak-to-peak (measured 10.9 px on a 32-wide grid, 5.2 px median on a 16-wide grid); the port currently spans ~20% (6.4 px / 3.0 px). Visually the original's bands are bold S-curves and the port's are shallow wiggles.

Slow the vertical cycle by ~25%. The original repeats every 6.25-6.50 s at a fixed row; the port repeats every 5.00 s (both measured by autocorrelation, and both stable across --fps 10/20/40). Equivalently, the y-wavelength of the undulation should be ~1.4 grid-heights, not ~1.2.

Remove the invented 'Columns' (sliderColumns) control, or confirm it is a deliberate addition. The original has no controls at all. The dial's default value (0.5) happens to reproduce the original's 4-band geometry, so it does not break the default look, but it is a control-surface mismatch: a user changing it (to 1-3 or 5-7 bands) leaves the original's design entirely.

Minor: the port renders ~10% dimmer and slightly crisper - mean brightness 56 vs 62, mean pixel value 105 vs 115, near-black pixel fraction 13.9% vs 10.8%, near-saturated fraction 14.5% vs 17.5%, saturation 0.925 vs 0.905. The band brightness envelope is a touch narrower/deeper than the original's; widening the lit part of each band slightly (or reducing the sharpness of the gap between bands) would close it. Palette family, band order and hue span are already exact.

Everything else is right and should not be touched: 4 bands with one full rainbow turn across the width, no horizontal scroll, time-based (fps-invariant) animation, deterministic/seed-independent, resolution-independent (feature counts fixed, feature sizes scale with the rig at 8x8 / 16x16 / 32x8 / 32x32), and a steady state at t=120 s identical in character to t=0.
